- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.5), model underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if price is trending down.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- Model frequently fails to capture mean reversion in 10–15 day horizons; if price deviates >2SD from recent 10-day average, apply mean-reversion bias correction.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +1 to -1) triggers model lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to avoid premature reaction.
- In 30-day horizon, model often underestimates downward trends; if sentiment is negative and price is falling, add 2–3% buffer to forecast to account for volatility.
